paths.description: Redirect destination and organisation/index archetype; establishes public purpose, navigation, content density and global policy.
Primary account-entry guidance archetype, representing the unauthenticated sign-in journey.
High-value tax guidance/content archetype and route into a core tax task.
Interactive HMRC service selector on the requested host, representing service-specific frontend policy and delivery.
Primary unauthenticated support flow: select Self Assessment and reach the live chat input and recovery controls.
Representative invalid GOV.UK route to test network/HTTP failure communication and recovery.

findings.summary: The service does not adapt its colour scheme to the user’s dark-mode preference.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot remains the same white and pale-blue light palette as the default capture; computed html color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, link, focus and form-control colours, following the dark-mode guidance.

findings.summary: Key pages miss the good LCP bar, and the organisation landing page has severe lab layout shift.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured landing LCP 4.22s and CLS 0.556; the assistant measured LCP 5.07s. The trace corroborated a responsive main thread (0ms TBT), so loading and layout stability are the main concerns.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the Lighthouse shift culprits and LCP dependency chain to reserve late content space and prioritize the actual LCP resource; remeasure under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The image-heavy organisation page transfers disproportionate legacy, non-responsive imagery.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 2.08MB of images out of 2.25MB total. The images primitive found 21/21 legacy-format images, no srcset, all below-fold images eager, and all natural dimensions over twice display width.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, add srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold images, and keep eager/high-priority loading only for the true LCP image.

findings.summary: The assistant selector ships avoidable JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Its HAR transfers 583KB of script. Lighthouse estimated 235KiB unused JavaScript, 81KiB unminified JavaScript and 35KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused bundles on the selector route, minify production scripts, and conditionally load the chat client only after a topic is chosen.

findings.summary: The assistant route triggers browser-platform hygiene failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated API, DevTools Issues panel entries, two BFCache failure reasons, and a best-practices score of 0.58.
findings.suggestedFix: Inspect the named deprecated call and BFCache blockers in DevTools, replace the deprecated API, and remove unload/cache blockers so history navigation can restore the page.

findings.summary: The assistant sets a long-lived cookie without the Secure flag.
findings.evidence: The cookie primitive found optimizelyOptOut scoped to .tax.service.gov.uk, Secure=false, SameSite=None and a 400-day expiry. HSTS mitigates many downgrade paths but does not justify an insecure cookie attribute.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure and an appropriate SameSite value on every cookie; reduce the preference cookie lifetime unless a documented need requires 400 days.

findings.summary: The assistant’s browser-enforced policy set is weaker than the GOV.UK landing page’s.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows a CSP containing unsafe-inline and no Permissions-Policy on the assistant, while HSTS, nosniff and clickjacking protection are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-inline once nonce-based execution is complete and add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy for capabilities the service does not use.
